title: Finite Kummer level of the Tate twist
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum and $A=A_{E,n}$ of
[def-pur-conventions]; write $e=e(E/\Ql)$ for the ramification
index of $E/\Ql$ and assume that $e\mid n$. With $v_\ell$ normalized
by $v_\ell(\ell)=1$ (so that $v_\ell(\varpi_E)=1/e$), put

$$
N=n\cdot v_\ell(\varpi_E)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1},
$$

the smallest exponent with $\ell^N\cdot A=0$; here $N=n/e$, and
$\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E=\ell^N\mathcal O_E$, so that
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\cong\mathcal O_E/\ell^N\mathcal O_E\cong (\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z)^{ef}$
with $e=e(E/\Ql)$ the ramification index and $f=[\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E:\mathbf F_\ell]$ the residue degree,
is free of finite rank as a $\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$-module. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
of finite-torsion module sheaves on the small pro-etale site of any scheme
$T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible,

$$
A(1)_T\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A,
$$

where $A(1)_T$ is the finite-level twist of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ is the etale sheaf of
$\ell^N$-th roots of unity, and $\otimes$ is over
$\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$. The isomorphism is compatible with the
derived tensor product and with base
change.

proof.text: Put $R_N=\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u\in\mathcal O_E^\times$; here $e$ is the valuation of $\ell$ in uniformizer units. Since $n=eN>0$, $\ell^N=u^N\varpi_E^n$, giving equality of the two ideals in the statement. Moreover $\ell^j$ is zero in $A$ exactly when $ej\geq n$: an element lies in $(\varpi_E^n)$ exactly when its uniformizer exponent is at least $n$. Thus $N=n/e\geq1$ is the least killing exponent, and $v_\ell(\varpi_E)=1/e$.

The finite freeness of $\mathcal O_E$ over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is part (3) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Write its rank as $d$. Reduction of a basis modulo $\ell^N$ identifies $A$ with $R_N^d$. To determine $d$, first reduce modulo $\ell$: $\#(\mathcal O_E/\ell)=\ell^d$. On the other hand $(\ell)=(\varpi_E^e)$ by step 1. The filtration of $\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^e)$ by the powers of $\varpi_E$ has $e$ successive quotients, each isomorphic to $k_E=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)$: the map sends $\bar a$ to $a\varpi_E^i$ modulo $\varpi_E^{i+1}$, and its injectivity follows by cancellation in the DVR of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Each quotient has $\ell^f$ elements by choosing an $\mathbf F_\ell$-basis of $k_E$. Every quotient fibre is a coset of the kernel, so multiplying the $e$ fibre cardinalities gives $\ell^{ef}$. Hence $d=ef$. The resulting basis isomorphism is only used to prove freeness and rank; it does not define the canonical sheaf comparison.

Set $L_T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$ and $M_{N,T}=L_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(R_N)_T$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (3), specialized to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, uniformizer $\ell$ and level $N$, $M_{N,T}$ is locally free of rank one over $(R_N)_T$; these are exactly the scalar extensions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. We verify that the particular map $\rho_{N,T}:M_{N,T}\to\mu_{\ell^N,T}$, $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a\,p_N(x)$, is an isomorphism, rather than merely using an unspecified isomorphism of the two lines. The balanced tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies $M_{N,T}$ with $L_T/\ell^N L_T$: the inverse maps are $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto a[x]$ and $[x]\mapsto x\otimes1$, with lifts of $\bar a$ chosen locally; changing a lift contributes $\ell^N[x]=0$. The inverse limit is sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Write a section $x$ of $\ker p_N$ multiplicatively as $(x_r)$, so $x_N=1$. Then $y_r=x_{r+N}$ belongs to $\mu_{\ell^r}$ because $x_{r+N}^{\ell^r}=x_N=1$, the $y_r$ are compatible, and $\ell^Ny=x$. Conversely $p_N(\ell^Ny)=1$ for every $y$. Thus $\ker p_N=\ell^NL_T$, and $\rho_{N,T}$ is a monomorphism. Trivialize $M_{N,T}$ and $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ together using (3) and (1) of the cited Tate-line lemma. The map between the two constant $R_N$-lines is multiplication by a locally constant scalar $a$; refine the cover until $a$ is constant. On a nonempty member of this cover, a nonunit $a\in R_N$ is divisible by $\ell$ and annihilates the nonzero constant section $\ell^{N-1}$, contradicting monicity. On an empty member both module sheaves are zero, so the comparison is already an isomorphism. Hence $a$ is a unit on every member of this cover and $\rho_{N,T}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the required projection formula without identifying the completed coefficient sheaf with the constant sheaf.

The two successive scalar extensions in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identify $A(1)_T$ with $L_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}A_T$. Here the explicit associativity maps are $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes ba$ and $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Since $\ell^N A=0$, the balanced tensor relations give mutually inverse maps
$$L_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}A_T\longleftrightarrow (L_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(R_N)_T)\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T,$$
$$x\otimes a\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a,\qquad (x\otimes\bar b)\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes\bar b a.$$
Changing a lift of $\bar b$ changes the latter by a multiple of $\ell^N a=0$. These formulas first define maps of presheaf tensor products and then of their sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; checking them on pure tensors proves that they are inverse. Compose with $\rho_{N,T}\otimes1$ from step 3. This proves the asserted canonical isomorphism $\alpha_T$, explicitly $x\otimes a\mapsto p_N(x)\otimes a$.

By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (1), $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ is locally free of rank one over $(R_N)_T$. On a trivializing cover, tensoring with it is the identity functor on module sheaves. Thus it preserves exactness: a section in a kernel can locally be lifted from the preceding term on that cover, and equalities are checked locally. This is flatness as defined by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] this sheaf in degree zero is K-flat. Consequently the ordinary tensor on the right of $\alpha_T$ is also $\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes^L_{R_N}A_T$, by [def-weil-derived-tensor], with the canonical augmentation given by the degree-zero model. Put $B_T=\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T$. On the same trivializing cover $B_T$ is $A_T$, so tensoring over $A_T$ with $B_T$ restricts to the identity on that cover. For any exact sequence, a section of a kernel therefore locally has a preimage from the preceding term, and these local image conditions prove exactness of its tensor sequence. Thus $B_T$ is flat over $A_T$; the isomorphism $A(1)_T\cong B_T$ makes tensoring with $A(1)_T$ isomorphic to this exact functor. Both are K-flat in degree zero by the cited bounded-above criterion. Tensoring termwise with either line therefore computes the derived twist of any complex of $A_T$-modules. Applying the derived tensor bifunctor to $\alpha_T$ gives the comparison naturally in that complex. The $R_N$-flat sheaf in the first calculation is $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$; the $A_T$-flat sheaves in the twist calculation are $B_T$ and $A(1)_T$.

We verify reduction over the constant sheaf $R=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$ separately. Use the coefficient resolution of [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] and the constant-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to form
$$C^\bullet=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^N}R],\qquad C^{-1}=C^0=R,$$
augmented in degree zero by $R\to(R_N)_T$. This is a resolution on the site: the coefficient exact sequence in the quotient lemma gives a sectionwise exact sequence of constant presheaves. Sheafification of presheaves of modules over the constant ring is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], and its terms are exactly the constant sheaves just defined. Thus the augmented constant-sheaf complex is exact, with the stated quotient augmentation. Each term $R$ is flat because $R\otimes_R-$ is the identity, by the balanced tensor relations [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus $C^\bullet$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Multiplication by $\ell^N$ is also injective on $L_T$: writing its sections multiplicatively as $(x_r)$ by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], if $x_r^{\ell^N}=1$ for every $r$, then compatibility gives $x_r=x_{r+N}^{\ell^N}=1$ for every $r$. Hence
$$L_T\otimes_R C^\bullet=[L_T\xrightarrow{\ell^N}L_T]$$
has only degree-zero cohomology $L_T/\ell^NL_T$, identified by the projection $p_N$ with $\mu_{\ell^N,T}$ in step 3. Its augmentation to the ordinary tensor $L_T\otimes_R(R_N)_T$ is the quotient in degree zero, and induces the identity on this cokernel; it is a quasi-isomorphism.

To check that this computes the specified derived tensor, rather than assume that one may resolve the other factor, take a bounded-above flat K-flat resolution $q:P^\bullet\to L_T[0]$ using [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Both $P^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$ have flat terms. The bifunctor and natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identify $P^\bullet\otimes_R C^\bullet$ with $L_T\otimes_R^L(R_N)_T$. More explicitly the arrows
$$P^\bullet\otimes_R(R_N)_T\longleftarrow P^\bullet\otimes_R C^\bullet\longrightarrow L_T\otimes_R C^\bullet$$
are quasi-isomorphisms: each has cone the tensor of an acyclic cone with the K-flat other factor. Acyclicity is the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the quasi-isomorphism criterion is [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Here are the cone identifications with their signs. Use $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ and $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+f(x),-d_Xx)$ for $f:X\to Y$. For a complex $K$, the map from $\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ to $\operatorname{Cone}(1_K\otimes f)$ is the identity on $K^i\otimes Y^j$ and multiplication by $(-1)^i$ on the shifted summand $K^i\otimes X^{j+1}$. In that second summand the $d_K$ coefficient after this map is $(-1)^{i+1}$ and the $d_X$ coefficient is $-1$ on both sides, while the component entering $K^i\otimes Y^{j+1}$ is $(-1)^i(1\otimes f)$ on both sides. For $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(f)\otimes K)\to\operatorname{Cone}(f\otimes1_K)$ the identity on both summands is a chain isomorphism: on $X^{j+1}\otimes K^i$ both differentials have coefficients $-1$ for $d_X$ and $(-1)^j$ for $d_K$. These calculations use exactly the total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Finally the tensor symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ for degrees $i,j$ commutes with the total differential. With $\epsilon:C^\bullet\to(R_N)_T$, the first cone is therefore isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon)\otimes_R P^\bullet$ after this symmetry, and the second is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(q)\otimes_R C^\bullet$. The cones of $\epsilon$ and $q$ are acyclic by the cited cone criterion, so the two tensor cones are acyclic by K-flatness of $P^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$, respectively. The augmentation square to $L_T\otimes_R(R_N)_T$ commutes, since both composites are $q\otimes(C^\bullet\to(R_N)_T)$. Therefore the canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison is the isomorphism just computed.

Finally choose the basis $A\cong R_N^{ef}$ established in step 2. Its basis inclusions and projections express $A_T$ as a finite direct sum of $(R_N)_T$ and give the resolution $(C^\bullet)^{\oplus ef}\to A_T$. Tensoring this resolution with $L_T$ gives the finite direct sum of the two-term complexes just calculated: balanced tensor relations identify $x\otimes(a_i)_i$ with $(x\otimes a_i)_i$, with inverse given by summing the basis inclusions, and these maps commute with the differentials and augmentations. Kernels and images of a finite direct-sum differential are the direct sums of the kernels and images, so the augmentation is again a quasi-isomorphism. Put $D^\bullet=(C^\bullet)^{\oplus ef}$ with this augmentation $\epsilon_A:D^\bullet\to A_T$. Its terms are finite free $R$-modules, hence flat: tensoring with $R^{ef}$ is a finite direct sum, whose kernels and cokernels are computed componentwise. It is bounded above, hence K-flat by the cited criterion. The two arrows $P^\bullet\otimes_R A_T\leftarrow P^\bullet\otimes_R D^\bullet\to L_T\otimes_R D^\bullet$ have cones isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_A)\otimes_R P^\bullet$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(q)\otimes_R D^\bullet$ by the explicit sign maps above. Each is acyclic by K-flatness. Both composites to $L_T\otimes_R A_T$ are $q\otimes\epsilon_A$, so this resolution computes the canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison for $A_T$. Thus $L_T\otimes_R^L A_T\to L_T\otimes_R A_T$ is the canonical isomorphism, and step 4 identifies its target with $B_T$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto p_N(x)\otimes a$. The chosen basis proves invertibility only; the comparison itself is defined without that choice. This calculation is entirely over the constant ring sheaf $R$, and makes no use of completed-coefficient derived reduction.

proof.text: We spell out finite-root base change on the pro-etale site. Let $h:T'\to T$ be any morphism and $m=\ell^r$, $r\geq1$. Put $W_m=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Z[z]/(z^m-1))$ and $V_{m,T}=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}W_m$, using the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$, the fibre-product universal property and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identify $V_{m,T}\times_TU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B[z]/(z^m-1))$: compatible ring maps from $B$ and $\mathbf Z[z]/(z^m-1)$ are exactly a $B$-algebra map from this polynomial quotient. A map from an affine scheme into this root scheme is exactly an element $z$ satisfying $z^m=1$, whose inverse is $z^{m-1}$. For any scheme $Q\to T$, cover $Q$ by affine opens mapping into affine opens of $T$; the maps determined by a global root agree on every affine open of each overlap, since their ring maps send $z$ to that same restricted root. They glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Conversely a morphism gives these compatible local roots, which glue by the structure-sheaf axiom. This proves that $V_{m,T}$ represents the root functor [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], without assuming $T$ affine. Apply [lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale] on each affine chart with $g=1$ and exponent $m$; $D(1)$ is the whole chart and $m$ is invertible. The affine-local criterion in [def-weil-etale-morphism] now shows that $V_{m,T}\to T$ is etale, since the displayed affine root charts cover its source and their bases cover $T$. It is an object of the pro-etale site by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; its represented functor is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical]. Finally the fibre-product universal property identifies $T'\times_TV_{m,T}$ with $V_{m,T'}$: a map into either object is exactly a map into $T'$ together with a compatible map into $W_m$. This identification retains the coordinate $z$.

proof.text:
For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, its base change $V'=T'\times_TV$ is the object used by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every sheaf $G$ on $T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the adjunction and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(h^{-1}h_V,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,h_*G)=(h_*G)(V)=G(V')=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{V'},G).$$
The represented presheaves are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical]. Write $\Phi_G$ for this chain of bijections. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] gives an isomorphism $\theta:h_{V'}\to h^{-1}h_V$ with $\Phi_G(f)=f\theta$. Let $\delta:h^{-1}h_V\to h_{V'}$ be adjoint to the map $h_V\to h_*h_{V'}$ sending $a:Q\to V$ to $\mathrm{id}_{T'}\times_Ta:T'\times_TQ\to V'$. Evaluating this adjoint at $\mathrm{id}_V$ shows $\Phi_{h_{V'}}(\delta)=\mathrm{id}_{h_{V'}}$. Thus $\delta\theta=\mathrm{id}$, so $\delta=\theta^{-1}$ is precisely the canonical isomorphism $h^{-1}h_V\to h_{V'}$. Apply this to the global root scheme $V_{\ell^r,T}$ of step 7. We obtain $\beta_{r,h}:h^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,T'}$. Under the Hom bijections its adjoint sends a root $z$ on $Q\to T$ to its image under the global-section ring map for $T'\times_TQ\to Q$. This is precisely the comparison map of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. That ring map sends $zz'$ to the product of their images and $z^j$ to the $j$-th power of the image. Thus $\beta_{r,h}$ respects the group law and the scalar action, and for $t_r:z\mapsto z^\ell$ one has $t'_r\beta_{r+1,h}=\beta_{r,h}h^{-1}t_r$. For $g:T''\to T'$, the ring maps for the two projections compose to the ring map for $T''\times_TQ\to Q$, so, under the inverse-image composition identification, $\beta_{r,h\circ g}=\beta_{r,g}\,g^{-1}\beta_{r,h}$. The projection for the identity map is the identity, giving $\beta_{r,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. These formulas prove the transition, identity and composition compatibilities explicitly.

By the universal property of the inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] defining the Tate object in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the compatible maps $h^{-1}L_T\xrightarrow{h^{-1}p_r}h^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,T}\xrightarrow{\beta_{r,h}}\mu_{\ell^r,T'}$ give a map $c_h:h^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'}$ satisfying $p'_r c_h=\beta_{r,h}h^{-1}p_r$ for every $r$. The map $c_h$ is $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear: for $a\in\mathbf Z_\ell$, its $r$-th coordinate on $ax$ is $(a\bmod\ell^r)\,\beta_{r,h}(h^{-1}p_r(x))$, by the scalar compatibility in step 8, and these are the coordinates of $a c_h(x)$. Equality of all coordinates is equality in the sectionwise limit. No assertion that inverse image preserves this infinite limit is needed. The inverse image of a constant sheaf is the same constant sheaf: it is the constant object functor, obtained by coproducts of the terminal sheaf and the relations presenting the set or module, and inverse image preserves the terminal object and these colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. For the finite rings $A,R_N$ the precise canonical coefficient maps are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] therefore extends $c_h$ to the usual finite-twist comparison $b_h:h^{-1}A(1)_T\to A(1)_{T'}$. By the explicit formula in step 4 and the displayed relation for $r=N$,
$$\alpha_{T'}b_h=(\beta_{N,h}\otimes1)\,h^{-1}\alpha_T.$$
Indeed both maps take $x\otimes a$ to $\beta_{N,h}(h^{-1}p_N(x))\otimes a$; pure tensors locally generate the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus the square commutes and $b_h$ is an isomorphism, since its other three sides are. For $g:T''\to T'$, the two maps $c_{h\circ g}$ and $c_g\,g^{-1}c_h$ have equal $r$-th projections by the formula for $\beta_{r,h\circ g}$ in step 8; hence they are equal by the limit universal property. Tensoring with $A$ gives $b_{h\circ g}=b_g\,g^{-1}b_h$, since both send $x\otimes a$ to $c_g(g^{-1}c_h(x))\otimes a$. The identity equations follow from $\beta_{r,\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ in every coordinate. The coefficient and tensor identifications used here respect the inverse-image composition maps by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor].

Finally [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] says that module pullback for the finite constant ring $A$ is exact, so its derived pullback is termwise inverse image with the coefficient action identified by the canonical ring isomorphism. Put $B_T=\mu_{\ell^N,T}\otimes_{(R_N)_T}A_T$ and $d_h=\beta_{N,h}\otimes1:h^{-1}B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{T'}$. For any $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with $R=A_T$ and $S=A_{T'}$, identifies the pullbacks of $K\otimes_A^L A(1)_T$ and $K\otimes_A^L B_T$ with $h^{-1}K\otimes_A^L h^{-1}A(1)_T$ and $h^{-1}K\otimes_A^L h^{-1}B_T$, respectively. Bifunctoriality and the equation $\alpha_{T'}b_h=d_h h^{-1}\alpha_T$ in step 9 give
$$ (1\otimes^L\alpha_{T'})(1\otimes^Lb_h)=(1\otimes^Ld_h)(1\otimes^Lh^{-1}\alpha_T). $$
The coefficient lines $A(1)_T,B_T$ are flat over $A_T$ and K-flat in degree zero by step 5, so these derived tensors can be computed by termwise tensoring $K$ with the lines. On each term the displayed equation is exactly the pure-tensor equation of step 9; the maps commute with the differentials because they act as the identity on $K$. Thus the ordinary and derived comparisons agree, naturally in $K$. This is the asserted joint compatibility with derived tensor and base change.
